**CAME and NICE static code formats**

[05/08/201105/08/2011](https://web.archive.org/web/20230319212549/https:/phreakerclub.com/date/2011/05/08) | [CodePerfectCodePerfect](https://web.archive.org/web/20230319212549/https:/phreakerclub.com/author/codeperfect) | 22:11

**Categories:** 

* [**Code grabber**](https://web.archive.org/web/20230319212549/https:/phreakerclub.com/category/kodgrabber)  
     
* [**Package formats**](https://web.archive.org/web/20230319212549/https:/phreakerclub.com/category/format)  
     
* [**Barriers and gates**](https://web.archive.org/web/20230319212549/https:/phreakerclub.com/category/kodgrabber/barrier)

Despite moral obsolescence, static codes continue to be used by manufacturers of gate and barrier control modules. As it turns out, static codes are also found in new alarm systems. Below are a few common code formats. The pulse durations are given for the code messages encountered.

**CAME and NICE formats** .

They differ from each other in pulse durations. To implement the transmitters, Holtek HT-12E encoder chips are used \- in this case, microswitches are installed in the key fobs, which set the key fob number. They can have one or more buttons \- the encoder chip allows you to implement from 1 to 4 buttons. They were also found in old pagers, where the button pins were used to encode the serial number. The pulse durations are set by a resistor in the encoder harness. There are encoders without a dial field; the serial number is stitched into the chip by the manufacturer.

![A graph with red linesDescription automatically generated][image1]

The code package consists of 12 bits. Before the start of the code there is a pilot period (consisting of 36 low-level intervals) and a start pulse (consisting of 1 high-level interval). It is the duration of the starting pulse that indicates what time interval is used when generating the signal. After the start bit, the sending itself begins, the beginning of the bit is from a low level. After the end of the last pulse, the codeword is repeated starting from the pilot period. When you briefly press the button, 4 code words are transmitted; when you hold the button, the messages are repeated cyclically (in series of 4 code words).

The possible number of code combinations is 4096\.

CAME pulse durations:

Log. “1” \- 640 µs low level (two intervals), 320 µs high (one interval)

Log. “0” \- 320 µs low level (one interval), 640 µs high (two intervals).

Pilot period – 11520 µs, starting impulse – 320 µs.

NICE pulse durations:

Log. “1” \- 1400 µs low level (two intervals), 700 µs high (one interval)

Log. “0” \- 700 µs low level (one interval), 1400 µs high (two intervals).

Pilot period – 25200 µs, starting impulse – 700 µs.

Other pulse durations are possible, but the ratio of high and low levels, as well as the pilot period and start bit are formed according to the same principle.

In this signal format, there are also 24-bit encoders, which differ from 12-bit ones in the principle of forming logical zeros and ones. An example of such an encoder is the Holtek HT-601x series chips, which differ in the number of buttons implemented. Essentially, the encoder implements the same 12 bits of code, but each logical bit is represented as two pulse cycles. In addition, the encoder implies three types of logical bits \- “one”, “zero” and “free” (“open”). The type of bit is determined by shorting the corresponding pin of the microcircuit to minus or plus of the power supply; “free” bits are implemented if the pin of the chip remains unconnected. The timing parameters of the transmitted signals are formed according to the same principle as in a 12-bit encoder.

![A diagram of a graphDescription automatically generated][image2]

**Format PT -2240 (Princeton)**

Encoders of this format consist of 24 information bits followed by a sync bit consisting of one high level interval and 31 low level intervals. The high level duration indicates the time interval that underlies the generated code. The timing parameters are set by a resistor in the encoder harness. The code may contain 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8 commands (button codes), depending on the type of chip. The code word does not have a preamble; the very first bit in the message is informational. The encoder serial number (address bits) are programmed by the manufacturer.

![A graph with red lines and black textDescription automatically generated][image3]

Pulse duration:

Log. “1” \- 1350 µs high level (three intervals), 450 µs low (one interval),

Log. “0” \- 450 µs high level (one interval), 1350 µs low (three intervals).

Synchronization bit – 450µs high level, 13950µs low.

**PT \-2262 format ( Princeton )**

The number of bits (24 pulse cycles) and the principle of forming time intervals are similar to the RT-2240. The main difference is in the formation of information bits \- the outputs of the encoder chip are used to obtain the serial number (address bits). Depending on the state of the pin (connected to the power positive, to the negative, or left unconnected), the bit can take the value 1, 0, or “floating bit ” . Each information bit is encoded in two pulse cycles using the same principle as in 24-bit Holtek HT -601x encoders. Depending on the connection diagram of the encoder chip, from 0 (transmitting only address bits) to 6 control codes (button codes) can be implemented, respectively, the number of address bits can be from 12 to 6\. Control code bits cannot be “floating”. When you press the key fob button, the encoder generates a message consisting of 4 code words; when you hold the key fob button, the messages of 4 words are repeated cyclically.

![A graph with red lines and numbersDescription automatically generated][image4]

The timing parameters are set by a resistor in the encoder harness.

Pulse duration:

Log. “1” – 1200µs high, 400µs low, 1200µs high, 400µs low

Log. “0” – 400µs high, 1200µs low, 400µs high, 1200µs low

"Floating" \- 400µs high, 1200µs low, 1200µs high, 400µs low

Synchronization bit – 400µs high level, 12400µs low.
